model_annotation: The plot illustrates how accuracy (ACC) varies with co-occurrence number for six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic (base-10) scale, with major tick labels shown at 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³; the plotted points appear at four increasing co-occurrence values spanning from the single-digit range up to a few thousand. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, ranging from about 37% to 67%, with regularly spaced tick marks every 5 percentage points (40, 45, 50, 55, 60, 65). The Base series is a black solid line with circular markers, increasing from about 38.4% at the smallest co-occurrence value to ~41.7% at the second point, ~43.9% at the third, and ending near ~44.0%. FT is a blue solid line with downward-pointing triangle markers, rising from ~39.9% to ~43.4%, then ~46.1%, and ending near ~47.7%. IKE is a red solid line with upward-pointing triangle markers, moving from ~42.9% to ~44.8%, then ~46.6%, and ending around ~49.4%. MEND is a brown solid line with diamond markers, increasing from ~44.5% to ~48.9%, then ~54.0%, and ending near ~56.4%. MEMIT is a purple solid line with pentagon-like markers, rising from ~43.8% to ~51.1%, then ~52.9%, and ending around ~54.7%. ROME is a green solid line with square markers, increasing from ~51.1% to ~57.3%, then ~62.4%, and ending near ~66.1%.
